topics.label: Course Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer opens the final lecture of the course by welcoming the students and outlining the key learning outcomes regarding cancer therapy approaches.

topics.label: Conventional Cancer Therapies: Surgery, Radiotherapy, and Cytotoxic Chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss conventional cancer treatment modalities, examining the principles of localized physical interventions alongside cytotoxic chemotherapy mechanisms, systemic toxicities, and drug resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting Intrinsic Cancer Cell Vulnerabilities and Checkpoint Defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies that exploit inherent biological vulnerabilities in cancer cells, including hormone signaling dependence, cell cycle checkpoint loss, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Targeted Kinase Inhibitors and Mechanisms of Acquired Resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on targeting oncogenic driver mutations using small-molecule kinase inhibitors, explaining their ATP-competitive mechanism, off-target effects, and multi-faceted resistance pathways.

topics.label: Monoclonal Antibodies and Antibody-Drug Conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the therapeutic application of antibody-based agents, covering naked monoclonal antibodies that block receptors and initiate cytotoxicity, as well as antibody-drug conjugates that deliver targeted cytotoxic toxins.

topics.label: Cancer Immunotherapy and T-Cell Engineering
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine approaches for engaging and enhancing adaptive immunity against cancer, encompassing immune checkpoint blockade, neoantigen recognition, bispecific T-cell engagers, and CAR T-cell therapies.

topics.label: Overarching Challenges, Historical Progress, and Future Directions in Oncology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the broader landscape of cancer treatment, assessing persistent challenges such as tumor heterogeneity, historical survival trends, emerging innovations, and clinical decision-making dilemmas.
